page_title: The Ops Identity Crisis — Susan Fowler

summary.name: The Ops Identity Crisis
summary.one_liner: An essay by Susan Fowler, an SRE at Uber, arguing that ops roles are changing as developers take on operational responsibility for the systems they build.
keywords: automate yourself out of a job
use_cases: Understanding the future role of operations engineers
Deciding whether a separate ops team is needed
Planning developer training for on-call and debugging
Reading an opinion piece on SRE vs software engineering
Making the case for developer ownership of production
summary.what_it_does: The essay argues that a separate operations organization is not needed if developers are ready, willing, and trained to run their own services, including deployment, monitoring, logging, debugging, and on-call. It describes three areas of expertise experienced ops engineers usually have: low-level systems knowledge, high-level distributed systems knowledge, and programming skills. It suggests ops engineers who automate their own work can move into building internal self-service tools and platforms. It concludes the identity crisis in ops is real but reflects positive change in the field.
notable: Written by an SRE at Uber drawing on Velocity Conf NYC discussions
Breaks down the three skill domains ops engineers typically have
Argues ops engineers can become platform engineers building self-service tools
caveats: Opinion essay, not a tool or product; no concrete software is described
Views are the author's own and reflect the 2016 conference context
